To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cells expressing a high level of chromatind-bound Mcm6* are committed, i.e., past G1 restriction point, and that the G1 restriction is a point in time, not a cell cycle phase.
there are two states of Mcm expression during G1 that can be identified by cytometry and separated functionally by passage of the G1 restriction checkpoint.
cells expressing a high level of chromatind bound Mcm6 in late G1 are committed to the cell cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the cell cycle and cell proliferation, and we are developing new methods to measure the cell cycle.
the identification and characterization of the G1 restriction (R) point, a critical regulatory checkpoint that controls the timing of cell division.
the identification of the G1 restriction (start) point.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high group represents cells that have passed the G1 restriction checkpoint and are committed to the S phase of the cell cycle.
the high Mcm6*/low PCNA* G1 state is post-restriction point and the low Mcm6*/high PCNA* G0/G1 state is pre-restriction point.
cells expressing a high level of Mcm6 are committed and have passed the restriction point.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cells expressing a high level of Mcm6 and/or Mcm2 in G1 are functionally committed to the cell cycle and are past the G1 Restriction Point.
cells with high Mcm6 and low PCNA are in late G1 just past the restriction point.
the fraction of pre-restriction point cells in a population of asynchronously growing cells is inversely proportional to the fraction of cells with high levels (i.e., post-restriction point) Mcm6*.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cells in the high Mcm6 group are committed, i.e., past G1 restriction point, and that cells in this group are in a state of readiness to enter S-phase, and are thus poised to respond to mitogens.
there is a clear correlation between the expression of chromatin-bound proteins and the cell cycle commitment of G1 cells.
there are at the very least two states of G1, a pre- and a post-restriction point.
